html:
A set of eleven wooden boats found buried near Butuan in Mindanao, the Philippines, carbon dated to between 689 and 988 CE. They are the largest group of early Southeast Asian plank boats ever found.

They are balangay, built in the old Austronesian way: planks were carved with lugs and joined edge to edge with wooden pegs and fibre lashings, without a frame put in first. The first was dug up in 1976, and others followed. They were built for trading voyages on the open sea.

Around the boats lay Chinese ceramics and goods from the Indian Ocean and as far away as Persia. They show that Butuan was a busy trading port well before the Spanish came. The Rajahnate of Butuan sent a mission to the Song court in China in 1001. The word barangay, the basic unit of local government in the Philippines today, is often said to come from the name of these boats, each of which once carried a whole community.
sum: A set of eleven wooden boats found buried near Butuan in Mindanao, the Philippines, carbon dated to between 689 and 988 CE. They are the largest group of early Southeast Asian plank boats ever found.
